page: Amazon Web Services r5n.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs through hyperthreading. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (F and VNNI) and AES cryptography. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB per physical core memory density. The instance has no local instance storage and relies exclusively on remote EBS volumes, while integrating a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark evaluations place the CPU multi-core and memory throughput in the mid-range of its peer group. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 34693.26 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 11039.0, while single-core performance reflects generational constraints with a weak stress-ng result of 1381.89 and a single-thread gzip compression rating of 23.66 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows read-only cached bandwidth reaching 2253.15 GB/sec and uncached 256 MB block transfers reaching 110.32 GB/sec read and 49.27 GB/sec write. In-memory application benchmarks demonstrate reliable scaling, registering 38.5 million Redis SET operations per second and 15658.37 PassMark database operations.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the r5n.12xlarge centers on balancing memory capacity and high network bandwidth against modest single-thread CPU performance and the complete lack of integrated local NVMe storage. Because I/O depends entirely on network-attached storage, application architectures must accommodate network latency for persistence. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU allocation coupled with 50 Gbps network bandwidth makes this instance economically practical for distributed in-memory data processing, caching tiers, relational database engines, and medium-scale model inference, where system memory volume and network throughput take precedence over maximum single-core compute performance.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for memory-intensive and network-demanding enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, it delivers 24 physical cores, 48 vCPUs, and 384.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, directing all storage traffic through network-attached EBS over its 50 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark testing reveals average multi-core and database performance, delivering 38.5 million Redis SET operations per second and 40674.91 on stress-ng multi-core, offset by lower single-thread compute metrics. The balance of high network bandwidth and an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core ratio makes the instance suited for large in-memory caching clusters, enterprise databases, ETL pipelines, and distributed analytics platforms where memory density and network throughput are critical architectural requirements.
